title: WPSB/505/2019 of N S GANGHARIA Vs UNION OF INDIA

paras.text:
UKHC010173172019
2026:UHC:5344-DB
1
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Bench No. 505 of 2019
03 July, 2026
N S Gangharia
--Petitioner
Versus
Union Of India and others
--Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Sandeep Tiwari, learned Counsel for petitioner.
Mr. Saurav Adhikari, learned Standing Counsel for Union
of India-respondents.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Per: Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
 Petitioner has challenged order dated
26.08.2019 passed by Under Secretary (Personnel-III),
Govt. of India, Ministry of Home Affairs. By the said
order, representation made by petitioner claiming
seniority on the post of Chief Medical Officer (Selection
Grade) w.e.f. 06.06.2000 was rejected.
2. Petitioner has challenged the said order
mainly on the ground that Dr. D.P. Singh, Dr. S.A.
Asgar and Dr. D.S. Chouhan, who also were serving as
Chief Medical Officers in 2001 and were promoted to the
post of Chief Medical Officer (Selection Grade) on
24.05.2001, were given seniority on the post of Chief
Medical Officer (Selection Grade) w.e.f. 06.06.2000,
therefore, denial of similar treatment to petitioner is
unjust and unsustainable.
3. Per contra, learned Standing Counsel
appearing for Union of India submits that meeting of the
Departmental Screening Committee was convened on

UKHC010173172019
2026:UHC:5344-DB
2
20.03.2001 which recommended 25 Chief Medical
Officers for promotion to the post of Chief Medical
Officer (Selection Grade) against 25 existing vacancies.
He submits that petitioner stood at Serial No.28 in order
of seniority amongst Chief Medical Officers, therefore, he
was not recommended for promotion against any
existing vacancy; the Departmental Screening
Committee also took note of 04 anticipated vacancies on
the post of Chief Medical Officer (Selection Grade) and
petitioner was recommended for promotion against one
such anticipated vacancy which was likely to arise upon
retirement of Dr. L.K. Banerjea w.e.f. 01.07.2001. Thus
he contends that petitioner was rightly given seniority
from the date of occurrence of vacancy on the post of
Chief Medical Officer (Selection Grade), against which he
was promoted. Thus, he submits that the claim staked
by petitioner for ante-dating his seniority from
10.06.2000 is without any basis.
4. Learned Counsel for petitioner then submits
that Dr. D.P. Singh, Dr. S.A. Asgar and Dr. D.S.
Chouhan were in Low Medical Category (LMC) at the
time of holding promotion exercise and these persons
regained their medical shape much later. The date of
their regaining medical shape is given below in tabular
format: -
Sl. No. Name Date of regaining
Shape
1. Dr. D.P. Singh 04.10.2001
2. Dr. S.A. Asgar 31.08.2001
3. Dr. D.S. Chouhan 29.11.2002
5. Learned Counsel for petitioner submits that

UKHC010173172019
2026:UHC:5344-DB
3
these three persons were given seniority w.e.f.
06.06.2000 even though they regained appropriate
SHAPE-I category for promotion upon expiry of the
relevant vacancy year.
6. In reply to this argument, learned Standing
Counsel for Union of India contends that aforesaid three
persons were considered for promotion against existing
vacancies and they were also recommended for
promotion against existing vacancies, available on the
date of convening the meeting of Departmental
Screening Committee, while there was no vacancy
available for the petitioner on the date when meeting of
Departmental Screening Committee was held. He
submits that since above named three persons were
promoted against existing vacancies, therefore, their
promotion was ante-dated to 06.06.2000. He submits
that there were vacancies available for granting
promotion to those three persons as their names were
included in the main panel, while petitioner was not
recommended against existing vacancy and he was not
recommended for promotion in the main panel of 25
Chief Medical Officers. Thus he submits that petitioner
cannot claim parity with those three persons, named
above.
7. Learned Counsel for petitioner then contends
that as per the applicable Policy, an Officer placed in
Low Medical Category can be promoted in the same
vacancy year in which he is recommended for
promotion, provided he regains Shape-1 and he cannot
be promoted in subsequent vacancy years. He submits
that these three persons returned to Shape-1 Medical
Category in subsequent vacancy year, thus the
promotion given to them was not proper and also

UKHC010173172019
2026:UHC:5344-DB
4
contrary to the applicable policy.
8. The said contention cannot be permitted to be
raised at this belated stage as the selection was held in
the year 2000; petitioner kept mum all these years; and
even in this writ petition, decision taken by competent
authority to grant promotion to above named three
persons as Chief Medical Officer (Selection Grade) has
not been challenged. In the absence of any formal
challenge to the promotion given to these three persons,
we cannot consider the contention raised by learned
Counsel for the petitioner that too behind their back.
9. The fact of the matter is that the vacancy
against which petitioner was promoted arose only on
01.07.2001. Earlier, there was no vacancy available for
the petitioner. That was not the case for the other three
persons whose promotion was ante dated, as there were
vacancies available for them as on 06.06.2000. Thus
petitioner cannot claim parity with them.
10. Having regard to the facts and circumstances
of the case, we find no valid reason to interfere in the
matter. The writ petition lacks merit and the same is
dismissed.
11. Pending application, if any, stands disposed
of.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
 03.07.2026
Rdang
